17-037.r: 1921 → 'Great Divide' / 'Demographic Divide' year: the only Census with negative decadal growth (-0.31%); after it population grew at an accelerating pace.
17-037.h: 1921: the one Census when India's population fell.

17-042.r: India's population grew phenomenally after 1951 (about 36 crore → over 102 crore by 2001) (A true); the 'Great Divide' year is 1921, not 1951 (R false).

17-045.r: 1951-2001: population density 117 → 325 per sq km (under three times); growth rate 1.25% → 1.97% (not doubled). Census 2011: density 382, growth 1.64%.

17-046.r: India (question period): high growth rate; likely to overtake China (done, per UN 2024); one in six people is Indian; BPL was below 40% (21.92% in 2011-12).

17-047.r: India's population → 1,028,737,436 (Census 2001) and 1,21,08,54,977 (Census 2011), so none of the options fits.

17-048.r: India's population, Census 1991 → 84.6 crore (846421039); Census 2011 → 1210854977; 1441.7 million in 2024, now the most populous country.

17-049.r: India (Census 2001, book) → 16% of world population on 2.4% of Earth's land; adds 18 million a year to world population vs China's 10 million.
17-049.t: Don't swap the figures: 16% is population share, 2.4% is land share.

17-050.r: Census 2011: India has about 17.5% of world population (not 18.5%); population 121 crore; increase of 18.1 crore in 2001-2011; highest density in Delhi.

17-051.r: Females in India's population (Census 2011) → 48.46% provisional, 48.53% final.

17-052.r: Most populous State (Census 2011, provisional and final) → Uttar Pradesh (199,812,341), then Maharashtra (112,374,333).

17-053.r: UP population (199812341, Census 2011) exceeds Japan, Russia, Brazil, Nigeria, UK, Germany, Pakistan; in 2001 only China, India, USA, Indonesia, Brazil were bigger.
17-053.c: (c) was right when asked; after Census 2011 Uttar Pradesh also outnumbered Brazil, so (b) fits too.

17-056.r: UP (Census 2001) → literacy 56.3%, density 690 per sq km, largest SC population in Sitapur; most populous district Allahabad, not Kanpur Nagar.

17-057.r: Smallest State by area → Goa (3702 sq km), not Sikkim; highest UT literacy → Lakshadweep, not Chandigarh; Maharashtra is second in population after UP.

17-058.r: Census 2011 order → Uttar Pradesh > Maharashtra > Bihar > West Bengal > Andhra Pradesh (undivided); so R (Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra) is false.

17-059.r: UP's share of India's population (Census 2011) → about 17% (16.49% provisional, 16.51% final).

17-060.r: Census 2011 population order → Uttar Pradesh > Maharashtra > Bihar > West Bengal > Andhra Pradesh (undivided); UP was top in 2001 too.
17-060.h: U-M-B-W-A: UP, Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal, Andhra.

17-068.r: Maharashtra → second in population (2011) and third in area (307,713 sq km) after Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

17-069.r: Bihar → third most populous State in both Census 2001 and 2011 (104099452), after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

17-071.r: Bihar's share of India's population → 8.07% (about 8%) in Census 2001 (82998509); about 9% in Census 2011.

17-073.r: More than one-third of India's population → Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Bihar.

17-074.r: Census 2011 population → Odisha 41974218 (smallest of the four), Karnataka 61095297, Tamil Nadu 72147030, Madhya Pradesh 72626809.

17-075.r: Census 2011 population → Maharashtra 112374333 > Bihar 104099452 > Madhya Pradesh 72626809 > Karnataka 61095297 (minimum of the four).

17-076.r: Chhattisgarh (135192 sq km) is larger in area than West Bengal (88752 sq km), but West Bengal has more people; both statements true.

17-077.r: Census 1991 population order → Maharashtra > West Bengal > Madhya Pradesh (then including Chhattisgarh) > Tamil Nadu.

17-078.r: Census 2001 population → Puducherry > Chandigarh > Mizoram > Sikkim (least); Census 2011 → Puducherry > Mizoram > Chandigarh > Sikkim.
17-078.t: Chandigarh and Mizoram swap places between 2001 and 2011; Sikkim is last both times.

17-080.r: From 1971-81 to 1981-91 growth fell in both India (24.66% → 23.87%) and Madhya Pradesh (24.65% → 23.50%).

17-081.r: Highest decadal population growth, Census 2011 → Meghalaya (27.9%).

17-082.r: Highest decadal growth 1991-2001 → Nagaland (64.41%), then Sikkim, Manipur, Meghalaya; in Census 2011 Meghalaya is highest (27.9%).

17-084.r: Highest growth 1981-2001 among given States → Nagaland (56.08% in 1981-91, 64.53% in 1991-2001); it fell to -0.6% in 2001-2011.

17-085.r: Highest decadal growth, Census 1991 → Nagaland (56.08%); in 2001-2011 Meghalaya highest (27.9%) and Nagaland lowest (-0.6%).

17-086.r: Lowest population growth 1991-2001 → Kerala; lowest in 2001-2011 → Nagaland.

17-087.r: Lowest decadal growth 1991-2001 → Kerala; Census 2011 lowest → Nagaland (-0.6%), then Kerala (4.9%), Goa (8.2%).
17-087.h: Kerala lowest in 2001; Nagaland negative in 2011.

17-090.r: Lowest average annual population growth 1981-91 → Kerala (1.34%).

17-091.r: Nagaland → only State whose population fell in Census 2011 (-0.6%): 1990036 in 2001 → 1978502 in 2011.
